# Proverbs 2 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** My-son, if you-receive my-words, and-my-commandments you-treasure with-you,

**2** To-make-attentive to-wisdom your-ear, you-incline your-heart to-understanding,

**3** Indeed, if for-understanding you-call, for-discernment you-give your-voice,

**4** If you-seek-her like-silver, and-like-hidden-treasures you-search-for-her,

**5** Then you-will-understand fear-of YHWH, and-knowledge-of God you-will-find.

**6** For YHWH gives wisdom; from-His-mouth knowledge and-understanding.

**7** He-stores-up for-the-upright sound-wisdom; [He is] a-shield to-those-walking-in integrity,

**8** To-guard paths-of justice, and-[the]-way-of His-faithful-ones He-preserves.

**9** Then you-will-understand righteousness and-justice and-equity — every good track.

**10** For wisdom will-enter your-heart, and-knowledge to-your-soul will-be-pleasant.

**11** Discretion will-watch-over-you, understanding will-guard-you,

**12** To-deliver-you from-[the]-way-of evil, from-[the]-man speaking perverse-things,

**13** Those-forsaking paths-of uprightness, to-walk in-ways-of darkness,

**14** Those-rejoicing to-do evil, they-delight in-perversities-of evil,

**15** Whose paths [are] crooked, and-devious in-their-tracks.

**16** To-deliver-you from-[the]-strange woman, from-[the]-foreign-woman [who] makes-smooth her-words,

**17** Who-forsakes the-companion-of her-youth, and-the-covenant-of her-God she-has-forgotten.

**18** For her-house sinks-down to death, and-to-the-shades her-tracks.

**19** All going-to-her do-not-return, and-they-do-not-reach paths-of life.

**20** So-that you-will-walk in-[the]-way-of good-ones, and-paths-of righteous-ones you-will-keep.

**21** For the-upright will-dwell in-[the]-land, and-the-blameless will-remain in-it.

**22** But-the-wicked from-[the]-land will-be-cut-off, and-the-treacherous will-be-torn-from-it.

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **2:1-5**: Extended conditional ('if...if...then') spanning 5 verses — characteristic of instructional wisdom. The structure emphasizes that wisdom requires active pursuit.

- **2:16**: Zarah (strange/foreign woman) — debated whether this is literal (foreign wife) or metaphorical (foolish wisdom). The parallel with ishah nokriyyah supports both.

— EMET
